literal: Before danger comes, the life of one who does not guard himself will be destroyed like a stack of straw before fire.
translation: The life of one who does not guard himself before danger arrives will be destroyed like a stack of straw before a fire.
modern: துன்பம் வருவதற்கு முன்பே தன்னைத் தற்காத்துக் கொள்ளாதவனுடைய வாழ்க்கை, நெருப்பின் முன்னால் உள்ள வைக்கோல் போர் போல அழிந்துவிடும்.
explanation: This couplet highlights the absolute necessity of foresight and preventive action. The word 'வருமுன்னர்' refers to the period before a mistake or danger actually manifests, while 'காவாதான்' describes a person who fails to guard themselves during this window. The poet uses a vivid simile, comparing such an unprepared person's life to a stack of straw ('வைத்தூறு') placed in front of a fire ('எரிமுன்னர்'). Just as dry straw is instantly and completely consumed by fire, the life of someone who does not anticipate and prevent faults will be swiftly ruined when adversity strikes.
